channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's economic growth reached 11 percent in eight months, says cabinet head
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's economy has maintained stable growth, reaching 11 percent over eight months, according to Adylbek Kasymaliev, head of the cabinet. GDP hit 1.397 trillion soms. Investments in fixed capital grew by 61.2%, construction by 61%, industry by 8.8%, and agriculture by 6.4%. The government also approved a state program for kidney disease prevention and treatment.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Pakistan establish new freight transit route via China to Pakistani seaports
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Pakistan have approved an agreement to establish a new freight transit route, aiming to expand Kyrgyzstan's transit potential and integration into international transport corridors. The route will utilize road, rail, and air transport to access Pakistani seaports like Karachi, Qasim, and Gwadar, fostering development in transport and customs infrastructure.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to receive up to $50 million grant for green energy transition
item.description: Kyrgyzstan may receive up to $50 million in grant financing from the International Development Association for the iFIRST project. The initiative aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 4 million tons over five years and improve energy efficiency. Funds will support reforms and potentially feasibility studies for hydropower plants.

item.title: Uzbek President gives interview to The Korea Herald ahead of state visit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev gave an interview to The Korea Herald discussing bilateral relations, high-tech cooperation, investments, and regional partnerships. He noted a five-fold increase in trade and over $8 billion in Korean investments. Future cooperation areas include AI, critical minerals, and semiconductors.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Bulgaria establish new phase of cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan and Bulgaria celebrate 34 years of diplomatic relations, entering a new phase of cooperation. Agreements were signed to strengthen ties, including a joint declaration and a foreign ministry program. Trade and economic cooperation is also intensifying, with plans to increase trade volumes and expand product supplies.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and China to build 56-meter bridge at Bedel border crossing
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's parliament has approved an agreement to construct a permanent 56-meter road bridge across the Uzongu-Kuush River at the Bedel checkpoint on the Kyrgyz-Chinese border. The new bridge aims to develop transport links and improve checkpoint infrastructure, replacing a temporary structure. Each country will finance its section of the bridge and access roads.

item.title: Russia's revenue from migrants increases, crime among them decreases
item.description: In the first six months of this year, labor migrants contributed 321 billion rubles (approximately $4 billion) to Russia's budget, primarily through work permits. Russian authorities report this revenue is 30% higher than the previous year. Concurrently, crimes committed by foreign citizens reportedly decreased by 40%.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea to Expand Cooperation on Critical Minerals and Technology
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held talks with South Korean President Lee Jae-myung in Seoul. The leaders discussed strengthening the special strategic partnership between their nations. Uzbekistan highlighted South Korea's role as a key economic partner, noting over 700 joint ventures and numerous projects in various sectors.

item.title: Energy sector employees compete in "TES Cup" sports event
item.description: Over 200 employees from thermal power plants across Uzbekistan participated in the "TES Cup" sports competition. The three-day event aimed to foster camaraderie and provide meaningful leisure activities for workers in the energy sector.

item.title: Three children of Uzbek women serving sentences in Russia returned to Uzbekistan
item.description: The underage children of Uzbek women imprisoned in Russian penal colonies have been returned to Uzbekistan. Diplomatic efforts facilitated the repatriation, with children arriving safely in their homeland.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev and wife accorded state welcome in South Korea
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and his wife were ceremonially welcomed at the South Korean presidential residence by President Lee Jae-myung and his wife. National anthems were played and honor guards inspected.

item.title: Tajikistan and UNICEF Discuss Environmental Program Cooperation
item.description: Tajikistan's Environmental Protection Committee met with the new UNICEF Representative to discuss cooperation on environmental programs aligned with the National Development Strategy until 2030 and the 2027 Joint Work Plan. Key areas include climate change, environmental safety, and ecological literacy for youth. They also explored using AI for soil pollution mapping.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Exports Decline 3.6% in Seven Months Amid Falling Gold Sales
item.description: Uzbekistan's exports decreased by 3.6% in the first seven months of the year, primarily due to a reduction in gold sales. This decline in gold revenue has impacted overall export earnings. In contrast, imports saw a significant increase of nearly 18% during the same period.

item.title: South Korea and Central Asia Launch C5+1 Industrial Ministers' Meeting
item.description: The first C5+1 ministerial meeting on industry between South Korea and Central Asian nations (Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan) was held in Seoul. They agreed to expand cooperation in industry, trade, and supply chains, focusing on trade development, industrial parks, strategic minerals, and digitalization.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Injured in Drone Attack in Russia Repatriated
item.description: An Uzbek citizen seriously injured in a drone attack in Nizhnekamsk, Russia, was brought back to Uzbekistan on September 13. The decision to repatriate was made after the patient's condition stabilized and Russian doctors granted permission for evacuation. The Migrations Agency, Uzbek diplomatic missions, and Uzbekistan Airways facilitated the transfer.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Officially Welcomed in Seoul
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev received an official welcome ceremony at the 'Chong Wa Dae' residence of the South Korean President on September 14. President Mirziyoyev and his wife were greeted by President Lee Jae-myung and his wife. An honor guard was present, and anthems of both countries were played before high-level talks commenced.

item.title: Tajikistan Celebrates 35th Independence Anniversary Abroad
item.description: Tajik diplomatic missions worldwide held events marking the 35th anniversary of Tajikistan's state independence. Officials highlighted the country's achievements and President Emomali Rahmon's role in building a sovereign nation. Receptions were held in Ashgabat, Turkmenistan, and Washington D.C., with participation from Turkmen and US officials respectively.

item.title: Uzbekistan Chess Olympiad: Favorites and Dark Horses Vie for Gold
item.description: The 46th World Chess Olympiad opens in Samarkand on September 15. Javokhir Sindarov, Uzbekistan's top player with a rating of 2778, is a key contender. He received the Olympiad torch in India from FIDE acting president Viswanathan Anand. His preparation is supported by the National Bank of Uzbekistan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Debt to China Revealed; Finance Ministry Says Repayment Possible
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's debt to China has been disclosed. A deputy finance minister stated that the debts could be repaid immediately, though a phased approach is preferable. The information was reported by Daryo.uz.

item.title: Remote Sensing Center to be Established in Dushanbe with Chinese Cooperation
item.description: Tajikistan's Communications Service and China's Great Wall Industry Corporation discussed establishing a National Remote Sensing Data Center in Dushanbe. The center aims to monitor natural and ecological processes, including glaciers, water resources, and disaster impacts. Cooperation in space technologies was emphasized.

item.title: Uzbekistan Announces 200 Construction Jobs in Germany with Competitive Salaries
item.description: Uzbekistan's Migration Agency and Germany's RRG AG are recruiting 200 construction specialists for jobs in Germany. The monthly salary offered is 2,500 euros. Applicants must be aged 18-39, possess relevant education and at least two years of experience. The employer covers German language training, visa, and airfare costs.

item.title: CSTO 'Border-2026' Drills Begin in Kazakhstan with Tajik Military Participation
item.description: The CSTO 'Border-2026' military drills have commenced in Kazakhstan's Jetisu region, involving approximately 1,500 personnel from Tajikistan, Russia, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan. The exercises, focusing on combating illegal armed groups, will continue until September 18 and utilize over 300 pieces of military equipment.

item.title: South Korean firm to invest $100 million in Uzbekistan for robot factory
item.description: A South Korean company plans to invest $100 million in Uzbekistan to build a robot manufacturing plant. This initiative is part of broader plans to increase joint projects in high-tech sectors like artificial intelligence, pharmaceuticals, and biotechnology.

item.title: Tajikistan delegation attends Interpol CIS meeting in Minsk
item.description: A delegation from Tajikistan's Interpol National Central Bureau participated in a meeting of CIS Interpol heads in Minsk, Belarus, from September 8-10, 2026. Discussions focused on strengthening international cooperation, enhancing NCB effectiveness, and expanding information exchange to counter transnational crime.

item.title: Kazakhstan hosts AI & Digital Bridge 2026 with international tech leaders
item.description: Kazakhstan is fostering an open tech ecosystem and seeks international collaboration. The AI & Digital Bridge 2026 forum in Astana, part of the 'Year of Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence,' will gather global tech companies, investors, and developers from October 1-3.

item.title: First 'World of Circus Unites Hearts' festival to be held in Dushanbe
item.description: Dushanbe will host the first 'World of Circus Unites Hearts' international festival from September 17-20 at the State Circus of Tajikistan. The event celebrates Tajikistan's 35th anniversary of independence, featuring artists from 14 countries to promote circus arts and cultural exchange.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Launch Two Waste-to-Energy Plants by Year-End, Six More by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to launch two waste-to-energy plants by the end of this year and six more by 2026-2027, involving Chinese companies with a total investment of $933 million. These facilities will process 3.6 million tons of waste annually, generating 1.6 billion kWh of electricity.

item.title: Russian and Tajik universities discuss expanding cooperation and promoting Russian language
item.description: Russian Deputy Minister of Science and Higher Education Konstantin Mogilevsky met with the rector of the Russian-Tajik (Slavic) University (RSU) in Dushanbe to discuss RSU's development. The meeting focused on enhancing cooperation with Russian universities, promoting the Russian language, and developing joint educational programs. Prospects for creating new programs and a Center for Professional Competencies were also considered.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Interior and Education Ministries enhance security measures for new school year
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Interior Ministry and Education Ministry are increasing security measures around educational institutions as the 2026-2027 academic year begins on September 15. Law enforcement will ensure student safety on roads, monitor traffic rules, and conduct preventive work. Drivers are urged to be cautious near schools, and parents are advised to discuss road safety with their children.

item.title: Lawyer seeks public help to cover damages for convicted Kyrgyz nephrologist
item.description: The lawyer for convicted Kyrgyz nephrologist Nasira Beyshebaeva is appealing for public assistance to help her pay over 2 million soms in damages awarded to a patient's mother. The doctor was sentenced to three years in prison. The lawyer stated the sum is unaffordable for the doctor and provided a bank account for donations.

item.title: Chubak aжы Jalilov Awarded 'People's Hero' Title Posthumously
item.description: Chubak aжы Jalilov has been posthumously awarded the highest title of 'People's Hero' of Kyrgyzstan. President Sadyr Japarov presented the award to his son, Abdullah Jalilov. The title recognizes his significant contribution to religious education and cultural traditions.

item.title: CIS Penitentiary Service Heads Convene in Kazan for Regular Meeting
item.description: The Council of Heads of Penitentiary Services of CIS member states held a regular meeting in Kazan on September 11, 2026. Representatives from Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan attended. The meeting focused on strengthening stability and security within the CIS.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes Building 'New Silk Road' with South Korea
item.description: In an article published in South Korea's The Chosun Daily, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed establishing a 'New Silk Road' with South Korea. He analyzed historical ties, current strategic partnership, and future priorities, advocating for a 21st-century route through advanced industries and transport corridors.

item.title: Juma Odina: A courageous Tajik writer criticized Communist Party policies during the Soviet era
item.description: Juma Odina was a courageous Tajik writer who criticized Communist Party policies during the Soviet era. His novel 'Guzashti ayyom' faced backlash, leading to the burning of 14,000 copies. He was expelled from the Writers' Union and died in Dushanbe in 1982.

item.title: Uzbek electricians and concrete workers sought for jobs in Serbia with salaries up to 1500 euros
item.description: Serbia is offering 1,000 construction jobs for Uzbek citizens as part of preparations for the 2027 EXPO exhibition. Electricians can earn 1000-1500 euros monthly, while concrete workers will receive 700-1200 euros. Accommodation and food are provided.

item.title: ABank Receives High Rating from Independent Sustainable Fitch
item.description: ABank has received an 'Excellent' rating from the international rating agency Sustainable Fitch for its Green Financing Program, developed with support from the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI). This independent assessment confirms the program's high compliance with international capital market principles and sustainable financing standards, paving the way for ABank's entry into the international green bond market.

item.title: Uzbekistan sees rise in court cases of violence against women
item.description: Uzbek courts processed 2,018 criminal cases related to violence and harassment against women in the first half of 2026, a 65.7% increase from the previous year. Of these, 1,624 individuals were convicted, and 2,146 women were identified as victims.

item.title: Saudi oil exports at risk as global supply could drop by 4%
item.description: Saudi oil exports face risks, with potential for a 4% drop in global supply, according to Reuters. The Tadawul All Share Index (TASI) fell 1.3% on September 13, marking its largest daily decline since early April.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host International Forum on Sustainable Tourism Development
item.description: Dushanbe will host the "Dushanbe International Tourism Exhibition – 2026" and the International Forum "City Integration in Realizing Sustainable Tourism Opportunities" from September 24-26. An organizing committee has been formed to manage these events, aimed at developing sustainable tourism, expanding inter-city cooperation, attracting investment, and promoting Tajikistan's tourism potential.

item.title: UK Ambassador: Uzbekistan's Independence Crucial for Britain, Discusses Reforms and Regional Security
item.description: As his mission concludes, UK Ambassador Timothy Smart reflects on his tenure in Uzbekistan (2023-2026). In his final interview, he discussed trade, investment, education, and security changes. Smart emphasized the importance of Uzbekistan's independence and territorial integrity for the UK and outlined prospects for cooperation with the Central Asian region.
